messages:
maria: Heads-up — enabling nsys timeline on prod batchers caused a sporadic 8-12% p99 increase in text-gen latency during the 02:00 window. I captured a run and attached traces.
kevin: ouch. did you run full-trace or sampling?
maria: full timeline (nsys) + NVTX. we needed kernel-level timings to see where switchbacks happen. ended up with ~60ms of extra wall time across processes — looks like instrumentation pauses on host->device syncs.
ray: can you paste the command and the exact options? also which model and batch sizes?
maria: command:
```
nsys profile -o prod_batcher_run --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none --force-overwrite ./run_batcher --model v2-medium --batch-size 8 --reqs 500
```
batchers were at ~60% util, kv cache warm.
amy: sample=none => full tracing. that explains the overhead. we should try sampling mode or CUPTI-based sampling. full traces are heavy.
kevin: agreed. but we still need kernel selection hotspots — sampling loses some short-lived kernels (e.g., memcpy+matmul combos). what's the cost vs insight tradeoff?
maria: quantified: full trace = +10% p99, sampling @ 10Hz = +1.3% p99 and found top-3 long kernels but missed micro-switchbacks near KV cache probing.
ray: maybe do hybrid: sample most requests and full-trace only when our async heuristic detects a switchback pattern. e.g., when KV probe latency > X ms or when batcher drops below throughput SLO.
amy: we can implement lightweight guardrail: detect "kv-probe storm" by tracking per-batcher probe time moving average, trigger full trace for N requests with TTL, and rate-limit to M traces/hour.
kevin: yes. propose params: probe_threshold_ms=1.5, cooldown=10m, max_traces_per_hour=6, sampling_rate=1/10 during normal ops.
maria: ran a sim with those settings — overhead stays <2% on spike windows, and we still capture the problematic probe runs.
perf-bot: perf-bot: known issue #412: CUPTI sampling accuracy on <cuda11.4 gives sparse kernel attribution. Recommend driver >= 11.7.
ray: good call. check driver on canaries.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolling config update to batcher nodes scheduled in 15m: toggles will be behind feature-flag safe_profiler_v2.
kevin: also need fallback behavior if profiler stalls a worker — add a watchdog that cancels trace after 3s or if CPU uses >85% for >5s.
amy: for data retention, only keep nsys .qdrep for N=10 traces, upload aggregated hot-kernel list to s3, scrub nvtx payloads for pII.
maria: one more edge: KV cache read loops are often memcpy+cmp branches — sampling misses the cmp. solution: add a micro-timer that emits an NVTX marker when probe latency > 0.5ms (cheap check) and ensure sampling captures those markers.
ray: sounds good. action items:
- kevin: implement sampling toggles + watchdog (ETA 3d)
- amy: retention + uploader + scrubber (ETA 2d)
- maria: instrument cheap NVTX probe-marker and sim (ETA 1d)
- infra: roll config with safe_profiler_v2 behind FF (start in 15m)
kevin: noted. will also add circuit-breaker to disable profiling if overall p99 regresses >3% within 10m.
maria: thanks all — attaching one small flamegraph snippet from the sampled run: https://s3.redwood/internal/prof/sample_flame_1876.png :thumbsup: 
ray: :eyes: great, check driver versions and let's run canary with the new config for 6h.
amy: I'll post the retention PR shortly.
kevin: ping me when canary starts, I'll watch SLOs.
maria: thanks — will update thread with canary link and any anomalies.
